A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlexAM, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. V1 includes two supplementary pages. V2 ends with references despite referring to supplementary training configurations and additional evaluations; those unavailable materials limit comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original motion-transfer, camera-control, object-editing and sparse-reconstruction experiments, including supplementary qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds VBench++ scores, a user study, comparative inference times and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: The core point-cloud encodings and VAE/adapter framework persist. However, Sections 3.1–3.3 replace the 19-channel motion-plus-mask description with 18 motion channels and separate appearance-mask conditioning, explicitly describe region-dependent denoising, and revise density-conditioning language. V1 already depicts separate mask tokens. The PDFs do not establish whether these are procedural changes or corrections and expanded documentation.

E1.justification: The three principal tasks and RealEstate10K evaluation remain. V2 adds explicit moderate and severe geometric-mismatch scenarios in Figure 11. VBench++ is used for additional metrics, not demonstrated new dataset coverage. V2's unavailable supplement prevents checking its training corpus against v1's OpenVid-1M/Koala-36M mixture; omission does not establish dataset removal.

E2.justification: Displayed comparator sets remain unchanged across the matched experiments. However, v1 Section 4.1.2 names both VACE and Wan2.2Fun for partial editing, whereas v2 names only VACE. V1 supplies no identifiable Wan-specific partial-editing result, so it is unclear whether an evaluated comparator was removed or the description was corrected.

E3.justification: V2 adds five VBench++ metrics for motion transfer, a randomized A/B study with 27 participants evaluating eight video pairs across five criteria, and an inference-time comparison using different model sizes and GPU counts. These substantially broaden evaluation design. The retained camera experiment still uses 100 RealEstate10K samples and the same pose-error formulas.

E4.justification: The three existing component-analysis questions remain. V2 adds a rider example to positional-encoding analysis, replaces the drawer depth example with two depth/scale examples, and introduces geometric-mismatch robustness and failure cases in Figure 11. The sparse-reconstruction evidence is retained, without a new quantitative component-ablation study.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new user-study sample sizes and randomization concern evaluation design, while preference percentages are point results rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds VBench++ results, user preferences, runtime comparisons and qualitative cases. Figure 5 reports 59% overall preference for FlexAM versus 35% for VACE, and 91 seconds on one GPU versus 348 seconds on two GPUs. Existing CLIP, camera, object-editing and sparse-reconstruction scores remain unchanged apart from display precision. V1's 71-second inference result has specified conditions that do not establish comparability with v2's 91-second result.

T1.justification: The cosine positional encodings, depth-colormap construction and camera-error formulas retain their mathematical substance. Separating the existing mask from the motion-channel count and explicitly writing frequency concatenation reorganize the representation rather than introduce new mathematical reasoning. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim unified appearance–motion control through precise, depth-aware, density-flexible point-cloud signals, supporting I2V/V2V editing, camera control and object manipulation. The revised contribution wording emphasizes masked-video conditioning already described in v1; the broad performance claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific limitations involving severe source–target geometric mismatch, lighting diversity, heavy occlusion and fast motion. It also explains depth failures through scale-versus-depth ambiguity and newly argues that the Spectral colormap improves depth sensitivity and convergence. These refine applicability and mechanism explanations without changing the central interpretation.

D1.justification: The supplied v2 loses substantial reproducibility information available in v1: rendering pseudocode, the 72,617-video training mixture, sampling strides, optimizer and training settings, and the 50-step inference configuration. It redirects training details to an absent supplement. V2 clarifies shared-VAE encoding, masking and density conditioning and reports comparative GPU counts, but these do not replace the missing specifications. The project code address remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning around Tora and newly cited MagicMotion, explains VACE's task-specific preprocessing more explicitly, and adds references including Go-with-the-flow, VBench++, DELTA, VE-Bench and MoGe. It replaces Qu et al.'s TokenFlow tokenizer citation with Geyer et al.'s video-editing TokenFlow. The central relationship to DaS and unified 3D control remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially reorganized around four limitations, and method and experimental passages are extensively rewritten for clearer conditioning and evaluation explanations. Numbered task subsections become run-in headings, and limitations precede conclusions. These are broad narrative and structural revisions beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 changes to a single-column layout, redesigns the teaser and pipeline, expands qualitative panels, and adds preference/runtime and failure figures. Camera and sparse-reconstruction tables become charts combined with qualitative results. V1's supplementary object-manipulation images move into Figure 7 alongside the retained scores, rather than constituting new results.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation through broader quality metrics, a user study and concrete failure cases, while improving several explanations and figures. However, the supplied PDF omits substantial training, rendering and inference information present in v1 and refers to unavailable supplementary evaluations. These empirical and explanatory gains coexist with a material loss of reproducibility and completeness, preventing a reliable overall quality judgment.
